title: Stay Calm. Remain Indoors. Dev Diary #5: Getting Sloppy
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
I’d always intended to use assets made by old friends and acquaintances, alongside work from the fantastic artists who publish through [Craftpix](https://craftpix.com). Some of these are people I know personally: friendly, talented artists working with very limited resources.

Following Epic Games’ recent announcement, I discussed this with friends, including some of the artists whose work I’d planned to use. Those conversations made me reconsider. Permission they gave me under very different circumstances isn’t something I want to take for granted.

I can accept my project going unnoticed. I can also accept it getting attention and receiving a negative reaction because of its use of AI.

What I’m uncomfortable with is the possibility of an artist earning subsistence wages getting dragged into that backlash simply because I used their assets. I don’t want my decisions about the project to become something they have to answer for.

So I’m replacing the externally made artwork with assets generated through imagegen.

It’s relatively basic stuff, but I’m very happy with the results so far.

I’m not a huge fan of “Here are my machine-generated assets—are they pretty, Y/N?” posts, so I wanted to share something useful I learned in the process.

Let’s talk parallax.

I hadn’t realized until today that imagegen could produce usable layers for a parallax background. Getting them to loop cleanly takes some work at the seams, but I’ve found that manageable, especially at pixel-art scale.

Parallax creates a sense of depth and motion by moving layers at different speeds: foreground elements move faster, while distant elements move more slowly. If those layers also tile seamlessly, you can keep the scene scrolling horizontally for as long as you need.

Once I had the assets prepared, getting the scrolling behavior working with coding assistance was straightforward.

If you have a background you’d like to bring to life, or your game feels visually flat, parallax might be worth experimenting with. Even a few layers can give a scene a stronger sense of distance and scale.
